paper: Balmer et al. (2025, AJ; arXiv:2503.13608, doi:10.3847/1538-3881/adb1c6), Sections III.2-III.3 and Table 1: NIRCam LWB narrow of 51 Eri, GTO 1412 observations 12 and 15 (two rolls), PSF reference HD 30562 in observation 14 (5-POINT-BAR dither), 2023 October; the planet is detected in F410M only.

settingSources.crFromSiaf: Paper III.2: the LWB narrow uncal headers carry wrong CRPIX; the mask position is taken from SIAF (spaceKLIP #182, in the pinned commit).
settingSources.stage1: Paper III.2: dark subtraction skipped, 4 pseudo-reference pixels on each edge, jump threshold 4. The saturation growth and the three- and four-group thresholds are not in the paper; they are the values of Balmer's own spaceKLIP script of the same period, github.com/wbalmer/aflepb_nircam_ddt aflep_nircam_epoch1_reduction.py.
settingSources.stage2: Balmer's AF Lep b script: outlier detection run. The paper does not state it.
settingSources.badPixels: Paper III.2: bad pixels the pipeline missed are sigma-clipped at 5. The method chain and its other arguments are Balmer's AF Lep b script (which clips at 3).
settingSources.padPixels: Paper III.2: the 400x256 subarray padded to 451x451 ([left, right, bottom, top]).
settingSources.spectralType: SIMBAD F0IV (Abt & Morrell 1995), a key of webbpsf_ext’s spectral table, as the model spectrum for centring; the paper names no type.
settingSources.align: Paper III.2: the central leakage masked with a rectangle of zeros and the square root taken for the shift estimate (spaceKLIP #183). The rectangle size is not given; msk_shp 8 is spaceKLIP's default.
settingSources.blur: Paper III.2: Gaussian blur FWHM = lambda / 2.3 D with D = 5.2 m before any interpolation; spaceKLIP blur_frames(fact='auto') computes exactly this.
settingSources.klip: Paper III.3: 51 Eri b is recovered in F410M only, with the image split into eight annuli and four subsections and reference-star (RDI) subtraction. The paper is inconsistent on the KL count: its text says 50 eigenimages, its Figure 4 panel is labelled KL=150; both are run, and with 90 reference frames pyKLIP cannot use more than 90.
settingSources.firstAnnulusOuterArcsec: Paper III.3: "the first of eight annular zones restricts the starlight subtraction to the inner 0.5 arcseconds". spaceKLIP’s dataset otherwise sets pyKLIP’s outer radius to the sum of the image’s half-widths, 201 pixels, which makes each of the eight annuli about 1.6 arcseconds wide; the outer radius is set so the first annulus ends at 0.5 arcseconds.
